questions.statement: I ___ dinner when the phone rang. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A phone call that interrupted a longer past action.

options.feedback: Was having is the past continuous and describes the dinner already in progress when the call arrived.
Had is the past simple and would report the dinner as a finished event.
Was have is not a valid form, because the progressive needs the -ing form.
Have is present simple and belongs to a repeated habit, not to a past evening.

questions.explanation:
The past continuous sets the scene of a longer action that was running when a short past action interrupted it: I was having dinner when the phone rang.
---

questions.statement: It ___ heavily when we arrived at the stadium. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: The weather at the moment the match started.

options.feedback: Rained is past simple and would focus only on the rain as a single event.
Was raining is the past continuous and paints the background of a past scene.
Rains is present simple, used for general facts about the weather.
Is raining is present continuous, which does not belong to a finished past moment.

questions.explanation:
A background that was in progress at a past moment takes the past continuous: it was raining when we arrived.

questions.statement: The lamps ___ one by one along the narrow street. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A writer describing the mood of a village at dusk.

options.feedback: Went out is past simple and would treat the action as one single completed event.
Go out is present simple, which would describe a repeated general action.
Were going out is the past continuous and suggests several lamps being switched off over a period.
Are going out is present continuous, so it cannot describe a past street.

questions.explanation:
One by one suggests a gradual action spread over time, and the past continuous is the tense that expresses that gradual past process.

questions.statement: Usually she cycled to work, but last winter she ___ the bus. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A speaker compares a past routine with what usually happens.

options.feedback: Takes is present simple and would describe the situation of today.
Took is past simple and would present the change as an isolated past act.
Is taking is present continuous, so it does not match last winter.
Was taking is the past continuous used for a temporary change inside a past period.

questions.explanation:
Last winter sets the whole contrast in the past, so the temporary deviation is expressed with the past continuous: she was taking the bus.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence in which the action was still in progress.
questions.context: Two sentences describing the same past event from different angles.

options.text: He was painting the wall when the lights went out.
options.feedback: Was painting is past continuous and keeps the action unfinished when another event cut in.

options.text: He painted the wall and went to bed.
options.feedback: Painted and went are both past simple, so the actions appear as finished and separate.

options.text: He paints the wall every spring.
options.feedback: Paints is present simple and describes a repeated yearly habit.

options.text: He will paint the wall next week.
options.feedback: Will paint is future simple and belongs to next week.

questions.explanation:
Was painting when the lights went out is the classic pattern of the past continuous: a background action still running when a short past event interrupted it.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: They ___ to the concert; they were listening to the radio. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A negative sentence about what was happening in the past.

options.feedback: Did not go is the past simple negative and reports a single finished decision.
Were not going is the past continuous in the negative, which fits a past situation in progress.
Not went has no auxiliary and is not a valid negative form.
Are not going is present continuous and cannot describe the past evening.

questions.explanation:
A past situation expressed in the negative needs the past continuous, so the sentence is built with were not going.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ___ you waiting for the bus? Choose the correct auxiliary.
questions.context: A short question asked in the middle of a past story.

options.feedback: Are is the present auxiliary and would place the question in the present moment.
Did builds the past simple and cannot be followed by the -ing form waiting.
Were is the past auxiliary of the continuous and agrees with you in this past question.
Do is the present simple auxiliary and does not match the past period of the story.

questions.explanation:
The question asks about a past moment, so it needs the past continuous auxiliary were plus the -ing form: Were you waiting?
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: At ten the chefs ___ the sauces when the delivery arrived. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A chef describing the kitchen ten minutes before the service.

options.feedback: Prepared is past simple and would report the sauces as already finished.
Prepare is the bare infinitive and cannot stand as the verb of the sentence.
Have prepared is present perfect and would point to the result in the present.
Were preparing is the past continuous and sets a longer action in progress before the delivery.

questions.explanation:
Ten tells a past hour and when the delivery arrived introduces an interruption, so the sauces were being prepared at that moment.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The driver ___ too fast when the lights changed. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A witness describing the moment before an accident.

options.feedback: Was driving is the past continuous and shows the action still unfolding when the lights changed.
Drove is past simple and would leave the driving as a closed event.
Drives is present simple, used for general facts and habits.
Is driving is present continuous, which does not fit the past accident.

questions.explanation:
When the lights changed is the interrupting event, and the driving behind it is the unfinished past action expressed with was driving.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: In the photo, three children ___ in the square at sunset. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A traveller describing a street she cannot forget.

options.feedback: Played is past simple and would reduce the picture to a single quick act.
Were playing is the past continuous and describes the scene captured in an old photograph.
Play is the bare infinitive and cannot be the verb of this sentence.
Have played is present perfect and would relate the scene to the present, which a photograph from the past does not.

questions.explanation:
A photograph freezes one past moment, and the past continuous is the tense that describes the action of that moment: the children were playing.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The officers ___ the suspect when the ambulance arrived. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A news report about what the police were doing.

options.feedback: Questioned is past simple and would report the questioning as already concluded.
Question is the bare infinitive and cannot carry tense in this sentence.
Were questioning is the past continuous and keeps the questioning in progress at the moment of the arrival.
Are questioning is present continuous and does not belong to a past report.

questions.explanation:
When the ambulance arrived marks a past interruption, so the questioning behind it was still running: the officers were questioning the suspect.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He always ___ at eight, but that evening he slept until ten. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A choice between a past habit and a single past interruption.

options.feedback: Was getting up is the past continuous and would describe an action in progress, not a habit.
Gets up is present simple and describes the habit of today.
Will get up is future simple and does not match any past reference.
Used to get up is the structure that states a habit which existed in the past and no longer does.

questions.explanation:
Always and that evening set a past habit and one exception; used to expresses precisely the past habit that has stopped.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: While I ___ for the tram, it started to snow. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A street scene while the rain kept falling in the background.

options.feedback: Was waiting is the past continuous and introduces the longer background action.
Waited is past simple and would make the wait a short finished act.
Wait is the bare infinitive and cannot carry the tense of the sentence.
Have waited is present perfect and would point to the present, not to that past afternoon.

questions.explanation:
While plus a past continuous clause and a past simple clause is the standard combination: I was waiting for the tram when it started to snow.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: While the power ___, everyone searched for candles. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A writer describing what everyone was doing during a blackout.

options.feedback: Failed is past simple and would present the failure as one sudden complete event.
Was failing is the past continuous and expresses a process unfolding during the blackout.
Fails is present simple and describes a general fact about the equipment.
Has failed is present perfect and would bring the result into the present time.

questions.explanation:
The blackout lasted a period during which the search took place, so the failure is described with the past continuous.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: When I was a child, I ___ to school by bike. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: An old habit that ended two years ago.

options.feedback: Was going is past continuous and would describe a single action in progress.
Go is present simple and would claim the habit still holds today.
Used to go states a past habit that is no longer true, which matches a childhood memory.
Am going is present continuous and has no link to the childhood period.

questions.explanation:
Used to marks a repeated past state that does not exist any more: when I was a child, I used to go to school by bike.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence in which the past continuous is correct.
questions.context: A single sentence containing two past actions.

options.text: We crossed the bridge and the storm broke.
options.feedback: Crossed and broke are both past simple, so the sentence loses the sense of interruption.

options.text: We cross the bridge every summer.
options.feedback: Cross is present simple and describes a repeated summer habit.

options.text: We will cross the bridge next summer.
options.feedback: Will cross is future simple and moves the whole sentence to next summer.

options.text: We were crossing the bridge when the storm broke.
options.feedback: Were crossing is past continuous and shows the crossing unfinished when the storm interrupted it.

questions.explanation:
The uninterrupted background action takes the past continuous, and the interrupting short event takes the past simple, which is exactly the structure of the correct option.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The soup ___ for ten minutes before I added the cream. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A cook describing the moment the sauce changed.

options.feedback: Was simmering is the past continuous and shows the soup still cooking during that whole stretch of time.
Simmered is past simple and would give a single completed action with no duration.
Simmers is present simple, used for a general fact about soups.
Is simmering is present continuous, so it does not belong to a finished cooking process.

questions.explanation:
For ten minutes before gives the duration of a past action that had not ended when I added the cream, which is past continuous territory.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Last July we ___ from sunrise until the boat left the port. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: Two friends reconstructing what they were doing on holiday last July.

options.feedback: Fished is past simple and would present the whole morning as one brief event.
Were fishing is the past continuous and covers the long uninterrupted activity of that morning.
Fish is the bare infinitive and cannot express any past reference.
Have fished is present perfect and would connect the morning to the present moment.

questions.explanation:
From sunrise until the boat left marks a long past period, and the past continuous is the tense that spreads an action across such a period.
---

questions.statement: The pupils ___ for the last twenty minutes of the exam. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A teacher describing the pupils during a difficult test.

options.feedback: Struggled is past simple and would report the struggle as a single quick act.
Struggle is the bare infinitive and cannot carry the past reference.
Were struggling is the past continuous and shows the difficulty lasting over those twenty minutes.
Are struggling is present continuous and would place the exam in the present moment.

questions.explanation:
For the last twenty minutes of the exam describes an extended past situation, so the past continuous is the correct tense.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that keeps the action unfinished.
questions.context: A choice of sentence for a past story.

options.text: We climbed the rock and we caught the storm.
options.feedback: Climbed and caught are past simple, so the sentence presents two finished acts.

options.text: We climb the rock every year.
options.feedback: Climb is present simple and describes a yearly routine.
Climbed is past simple, and the sentence offers no background for the interruption.

options.text: We were climbing the rock when the storm caught us.
options.feedback: Were climbing is past continuous and shows the climb still going on when the storm arrived.

questions.explanation:
Only the past continuous keeps the climbing running at the moment the storm arrives, which is the meaning the story needs.
